newsitem.title: USA: Half of central Illinois gets rain, more coming.
newsitem.headline: Half of central Illinois gets rain, more coming.

text.p: Rains fell across half of central Illinois over the weekend and early Monday and more precipitation was expected, meteorologists said.

"In our estimation, the dry area of central Illinois is a heck of a lot smaller than it was Friday," said Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis. "Definitely there are some dry pockets left but we see numerous reports of the smaller stations in Illinois getting an inch."
Meteorologists said Springfield, Ill., received 0.88 inch by early Monday while Peoria got 0.40 inch and St. Louis saw 1.50 inch.

"We had a couple of different systems," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp. "One came through on Saturday that produced anywhere from .25 to 1.00 inch, in and around the Moline area, Springfield and St. Louis. Another system is affecting parts of central and northern Illinois this morning."
Forecasts called for more rains through Tuesday night.
"We're still looking at the potential for an additional 0.30 to 1.50 inches in the dry areas of central Illinois in the next 24 to 48 hours with coverage of 65 percent," Palmerino said.
Weather Express Inc Chief Forecaster Fred Gesser predicted 0.50 to 1.50 inch with 60 to 70 percent coverage.
"Temperature-wise, behind this system we cool back down into the lower 80s in the Corn Belt," Gesser said.
Solberg of Freese-Notis put coverage at 60 to 80 percent.

"We have excellent chances for rain in those dry areas, 0.50 to 1.50 inch in the next 36 hours, basically across most of Illinois," Solberg said. "There are definitely some areas that got missed but there's an excellent chance for them in the next days."
Gesser said temperatures would warm up again by Friday with the next rain event expected late Friday through Tuesday.
